newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-YOUNG SPURS GLOUCESTERSHIRE WITH RAPID 89.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-YOUNG SPURS GLOUCESTERSHIRE WITH RAPID 89.

text.p: Tasmanian all-rounder Shaun Young lashed an unbeaten 89 from 94 deliveries to set up Gloucestershire for a 55-run Sunday League win over Middlesex at Bristol.
Young was close to his second league century in three weeks when Gloucestershire's innings closed on 232 for six after their 40 overs.
The Tasmanian, playing his first season of county cricket, struck a six and nine fours and put on 116 in 17 overs for the third wicket with Monte Lynch, who hit 53 in 55 balls.

Paceman Jon Lewis put Gloucestershire in control with three wickets in four overs as Middlesex slipped to 66 for five. Owais Shah, who reached a half-century off 51 balls on his way to 65 not out, checked the slide but his side ended on 177 for six.
Surrey pace bowler Martin Bicknell hit his maiden league half-century but the defending champions still lost to Worcestershire by seven wickets.

Bicknell hit seven fours in an unbeaten 57 after Surrey collapsed to 36 for seven and were subsequently 59 for eight. Pakistan off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq (29) put on 83 with Bicknell to lift Surrey to 157 all out at Worcester.
Gavin Haynes caused Surrey's problems with a league best four for 13 and made a valuable 47 not out as Worcestershire secured their third win of the season with 8.3 overs in hand.
Kent, defending a modest total of 141 against Durham, hit back to snatch victory by 16 runs at Darlington.

Durham looked set for an emphatic win when John Morris hit 47 at a run a ball. But from 58 for one at the start of the 13th over, Durham collapsed to 125 all out, their last five wickets tumbling for seven runs.
Lancashire stayed top of the table despite their match against Glamorgan at Old Trafford being washed out. They have 26 points -- two more than Essex, who did not have a fixture, and Kent.
